evidence.AC1: POST /todos with {"title":"past","dueDate":"2026-10-14"} returned 201 and the todo carried dueDate "2026-10-14". The same worked for 2026-10-15 and 2026-10-16. A POST without dueDate returned 201 with dueDate null. The date is a plain YYYY-MM-DD string with no time.
evidence.AC2: PATCH /todos/4 with {"dueDate":"2026-10-01"} returned 200 and the date was set. PATCH with {"dueDate":null} returned 200 and dueDate became null. PATCH with a new date set it again.
evidence.AC3: POST with dueDate "2026-02-30", "15.10.2026", "2026-10-15T10:00:00Z" and 123 each returned 400 with an error message. PATCH with dueDate "2026-02-30" also returned 400.
evidence.AC4: Today is 2026-10-15. Test data: a todo due yesterday, one due today, one due tomorrow, one with no date (later given the past date 2026-10-01), and one with a past date marked done. GET /todos?overdue=true returned only the todo due 2026-10-14 and the todo due 2026-10-01. It excluded the one due today, the one due tomorrow, the done one with a past date, and todos without a date (before the date was set).
evidence.AC5: The page at / listed each todo with its date, for example "past (fällig: 14.10.2026) überfällig", "today (fällig: 15.10.2026)" and "future (fällig: 16.10.2026)". A todo with no due date would show no date text, since the page only adds it when dueDate is set. I did not check that case in the browser.
evidence.AC6: In the page snapshot, "überfällig" appeared only on the todo due 14.10.2026 and the one due 01.10.2026. The todos due today, due tomorrow, and done with a past date had no marker.
evidence.AC7: The page has a button labelled "nur überfällige". After I clicked it, the list showed only the two overdue todos (due 14.10.2026 and 01.10.2026).
